definitions.gloss: steep slope; steep incline; sharp gradient
definitions.explanation: A slope or gradient that is sharply angled. Used in geography, civil engineering, mountaineering, and disaster prevention contexts.

examples.japanese: {急傾斜|きゅうけいしゃ}の{道|みち}を{登|のぼ}った。
examples.english: I climbed a steeply sloping road.

examples.japanese: {急傾斜|きゅうけいしゃ}{地|ち}では{土砂崩|どしゃくず}れの{危険|きけん}がある。
examples.english: There is a risk of landslides on steep slopes.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{急傾斜|きゅうけいしゃ}が{多|おお}く、{大雨|おおあめ}の{際|さい}には{避難|ひなん}{勧告|かんこく}が{出|だ}されることがある。
examples.english: This area has many steep slopes, and evacuation advisories may be issued during heavy rain.

notes:
A compound of {急|きゅう} (steep, sudden) and {傾斜|けいしゃ} (slope, incline, tilt). Often appears in disaster prevention ({防災|ぼうさい}) contexts, as steep slopes are prone to landslides and mudflows during heavy rain.

Japan's mountainous terrain means {急傾斜地|きゅうけいしゃち} (steep slope areas) are officially designated and monitored under the {急傾斜地崩壊対策事業|きゅうけいしゃちほうかいたいさくじぎょう} (Steep Slope Collapse Countermeasure Program).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {急傾斜地|きゅうけいしゃち}: steep slope area
- {急傾斜|きゅうけいしゃ}の{斜面|しゃめん}: steeply inclined hillside
- {急傾斜|きゅうけいしゃ}を{下|くだ}る: to descend a steep slope
- {急傾斜|きゅうけいしゃ}{崩壊|ほうかい}: steep slope collapse

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {傾斜|けいしゃ}: slope, incline — the general term without implying steepness
- {急坂|きゅうざか}: steep hill — a steep hill on a road, more colloquial
- {崖|がけ}: cliff — a near-vertical drop, steeper than {急傾斜|きゅうけいしゃ}
